source_text: Circumcision removes the foreskin, which harbors a subpreputial space prone to bacterial colonization and microtears during intercourse that facilitate pathogen entry; post-circumcision, the exposed glans undergoes keratinization, forming a thicker epithelial layer that reduces susceptibility to abrasions and viral adhesion sites such as Langerhans cells concentrated in the inner foreskin. [94] [95]
